overview: Three-clinic diagnostic accuracy study of an automated urgent-message flag in silent mode, with random sampling of portal messages and an adjudicated two-clinician reference standard.
population: Portal messages to clinicians at clinics A, B and C from November 2026, sampled at random within each clinic.
exposure: Index test: the vendor's flag (urgent or not urgent), recorded silently. Reference standard: two clinicians rate each sampled message for same-day attention blind to the flag, with a third adjudicating disagreement.
procedures: Weekly random sample of about 200 messages across the three clinics, proportional to volume; written urgency definition with examples; calibration session before rating; the informatics nurse extracts messages and flags under the privacy approval.

outcomes.name: Sensitivity for urgent messages
outcomes.measure: Proportion of reference-standard urgent messages flagged urgent
outcomes.why: A missed urgent message is the main harm.

outcomes.name: Specificity
outcomes.measure: Proportion of non-urgent messages not flagged

outcomes.name: Sensitivity by clinic and language
outcomes.measure: Sensitivity within each clinic and for messages in languages other than English

outcomes.name: Reference standard agreement
outcomes.measure: Kappa between the two raters before adjudication
outcomes.why: Checks the reliability of the truth.

outcomes.name: Missed urgent messages
outcomes.measure: Content and outcome of each false negative, reviewed by a clinician
outcomes.why: Shows what the flag would have missed.

feasibility: About 200 sampled messages per week; two reviewers at two hours per week each can rate them.

flags: Subgroups limited to clinic and language
parsimony.simplestPath: One index test, one reference standard, one primary accuracy measure.

summary: Three-clinic accuracy protocol with random sampling and adjudication.
